headline: New model ramp lifts revenue as annual losses narrow
summary_short: Rivian's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $1,658M (+27% y/y, +20% q/q) on 12,194 vehicle deliveries (+14% y/y) as R2 ramped; operating loss narrowed to $836M from $1,114M y/y, but net loss widened q/q to $833M after Q1 booked a one-off $506M gain on the Mind Robotics deconsolidation.
summary_long: Automotive revenue grew on 14% higher y/y deliveries (12,194 units) and $103M more regulatory-credit revenue, offset by lower ASP from commercial-van/R2 mix. Cost of revenue fell y/y despite higher volumes on van mix, per-unit cost gains, and an IEEPA tariff refund booked against COGS; the ramp still added ~$100M of incremental cost. Software & services revenue rose 37% y/y on Autonomy+'s April launch and VW joint-venture work. Operating loss improved q/q (-$836M vs -$881M), but net loss widened because Q1 booked a now-nonrecurring $506M gain on the Mind Robotics deconsolidation. Cash rose to $3,592M; equity rose to $5,127M on VW/Uber share issuances. FY2026 guidance: deliveries raised to 65,000-70,000 units, EBITDA-loss outlook narrowed to $1.8-2.0B, capex cut to $1.7-1.8B.

drivers.explanation: R2 production ramp drove deliveries and revenue higher; core operating loss narrowed both y/y and q/q, though the reported net loss widened q/q against a Q1 that included a one-off gain.

Automotive revenue rose on a 14% y/y delivery increase and $103M more regulatory-credit revenue, partly offset by lower ASP from higher commercial-van/R2 mix; software & services revenue +37% y/y on Autonomy+'s April launch and VW JV development work.

Y/y decline despite higher volumes, driven by higher commercial-van mix reducing conversion costs, improved per-unit material/warranty costs, and an IEEPA tariff refund receivable recorded against COGS.
Automotive gross losses improved on volume, regulatory credits, and the tariff refund, partly offset by ~$100M of incremental cost from the R2 ramp; software & services gross profit rose 67% y/y.
Q/q widening despite an improving operating loss: Q1 FY2026 booked a $506M gain on the Mind Robotics deconsolidation in "Other (expense) income, net" that did not recur in Q2.
Q/q increase reflects 63M shares issued to Volkswagen Group on achieved Testing Milestones and 20M shares issued to Uber under its Subscription Agreement, plus stock-based compensation.
